title: A session that writes an allow rule to settings.local.json is asked whether it belongs in the shared settings.json
why: Owner asks whether sessions add permission allowances to local settings when they should be global.
source: Consultant 20:20 CST Nov 13, from the owner's chat 20:16; unmeasured, since cloud sessions' local files are not readable from there.
note: Filed 20:17 CST Nov 13. Owner 20:16 CST Nov 13 (relayed): sessions may add allowances locally that should be global. Unmeasured: how often it happens. Fix: when a session writes an allow rule to settings.local.json, a guard asks whether it belongs in the shared settings.json and routes it to a lane PR. A guard; the lane measures first (read settings.local.json files that are readable), then test-author red case, builder, reviewer. Needs a lane. Lane started 20:18 CST Nov 13 (coordinator): session_013NEJL2mJoAeFDsLisvHPEE (Sonnet, medium; searches open PRs for a duplicate first). OWNER-FLAGGED VERY IMPORTANT, owner 20:19 CST Nov 13 (relayed by the consultant 20:24; triage did not see the chat): "triage/u/coordinator/batch runner shd also check if they have unique allows that r local and ought to be global (local-allow-goes-global) v important". Each standing session reads its settings.local.json files and lists entries the shared settings.json lacks, with a pick per entry (global, keep local with a reason, or drop); change nothing yet. Reads so far: triage (this session) found no settings.local.json anywhere it can see (~/.claude, claude-settings, its worktree, joyous, ios-adblock); three allow entries in the installed ~/.claude/settings.json are not in the shared settings.json (merge * --confirm, merge * --confirm *, merge --role batch-runner), and all three come from the shared merge/cloud_allow.json, so they are not local. Coordinator: no settings.local.json in its session (20:20).
